articles.title: Indonesia Ferry Fire Tragedy: 5 Dead, Hundreds Rescued as Blaze Engulfs KM Barcelona VA
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: A catastrophic fire broke out aboard Indonesian passenger ferry KM Barcelona VA on July 20, 2025, as it sailed from the Talaud Islands to Manado Port in North Sulawesi. The blaze erupted around 1:30 PM near Talise Island, forcing over 300 passengers and crew into the sea.

body.html:
A catastrophic fire broke out aboard Indonesian passenger ferry KM Barcelona VA on July 20, 2025, as it sailed from the Talaud Islands to Manado Port in North Sulawesi. The blaze erupted around 1:30 PM near Talise Island, forcing over 300 passengers and crew into the sea.

At least 5 people, including a pregnant woman, have died. More than 280 have been rescued so far, though dozens suffered burns and smoke inhalation, with at least 18 seriously injured. The number of missing remains uncertain as the passenger manifest has yet to be fully reconciled.

Dramatic videos circulating online show terrified passengers — including children — jumping into the ocean wearing life jackets or clinging to debris. One livestream showed a passenger holding a baby while pleading for help.

The rescue operation, led by Indonesia’s National Search and Rescue Agency with support from Navy ships, fishing boats, and nearby ferries, is ongoing. Locals have also joined the effort, helping pull survivors from the water.

The cause of the fire is still under investigation, with early reports pointing to possible electrical faults, engine failure, or a fuel leak. The ferry had already been delayed the previous day due to a storm, raising further concerns about its condition.

Authorities have urged families to stay calm as search and recovery efforts continue. The tragedy highlights persistent challenges in maritime safety across the region.

articles.title: RPF Constable Saves Elderly Man From Falling Under Moving Train at Betul Station
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: At Betul railway station in Madhya Pradesh, RPF constable Satya Prakash Rajurkar saved the life of a 66-year-old man who slipped while trying to board a moving train. The elderly passenger was engrossed in his mobile phone and missed boarding the train while it was stationary.

body.html:
At Betul railway station in Madhya Pradesh, RPF constable Satya Prakash Rajurkar saved the life of a 66-year-old man who slipped while trying to board a moving train.

The elderly passenger was engrossed in his mobile phone and missed boarding the train while it was stationary. When he realised and ran to catch it as it moved, he lost balance and fell. The alert RPF constable immediately pulled him to safety, preventing a tragedy.

Passengers are advised to avoid distractions like mobile phones at stations to ensure their safety.

articles.title: Bareilly Shocker: Driver Drags Home Guard on Car Bonnet for 5 KM, Flees
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: In a shocking incident in Bareilly, Uttar Pradesh, a driver trying to evade police checking dragged a home guard on the bonnet of his car for nearly 5 kilometres before throwing him off and fleeing.

body.html:
In a shocking incident in Bareilly, Uttar Pradesh, a driver trying to evade police checking dragged a home guard on the bonnet of his car for nearly 5 kilometres before throwing him off and fleeing.

The incident occurred at Chaupala bridge in Kotwali area when the home guard tried to stop the car during routine checking. To save himself from being crushed, the home guard climbed onto the bonnet, but the driver kept speeding through the city with him clinging on.

The driver finally threw the home guard at Mission Compound and fled. Police are tracing the accused using the car’s registration number. A video of the incident has since gone viral.

articles.title: Ajmer Sinks: Torrential Rain Turns Streets Into Lakes, Hospitals Flooded
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: Ajmer, Rajasthan — Torrential rain in the foothills of Aravali late at night brought the city to a standstill, flooding streets and homes. Low-lying areas went under water as Ana Sagar Lake overflowed, leaving residents stranded. Nala Bazar, Kesarganj and Bajranggarh saw heavy water flow.

body.html:
Ajmer, Rajasthan — Torrential rain in the foothills of Aravali late at night brought the city to a standstill, flooding streets and homes. Low-lying areas went under water as Ana Sagar Lake overflowed, leaving residents stranded.

Nala Bazar, Kesarganj and Bajranggarh saw heavy water flow. Water entered homes, shops, parking lots; goods worth thousands damaged.

Jawaharlal Nehru Hospital’s emergency unit flooded; patients shifted. Schools submerged, holidays declared. Power cuts, mobile networks down; residents struggled for basic services.

NDRF, SDRF and locals carried out rescue operations; video of devotees being saved went viral. IMD issued a red alert; ‘Ajmer Flood’ trended on social media as people shared help and updates.
